text.p: 1615 GMT - Swiss shares closed lower on Monday in a consolidation of last week's steep rise, dealers said.
They also said the profit-taking was normal considering last week's bull run.
A weaker German share market and the easier dollar also weighed on Swiss stocks and on industrials shares in particular, they noted.
* Main focus was on UBS which rose and on CS Holding, which declined, traders said.
Swiss shares closed lower on Monday in a consolidation of last week's steep rise.
A weaker German share market and an easier dollar also weighed on Swiss stocks in general and on industrials shares in particular, share traders said.
The broad SPI index was down 3.07 points to 2,483.66 and the blue-chip SMI fell 9.6 points to 3,888.3.
The main focus during today's session were bank groups UBS and CS Holding.
Dealers also watched German Telecom first trading day, but said it did not influence business.
CS Holding, which released its nine-month interim report, was down 1.50 Swiss francs to 134.75.
The weakness reflected investor disappointment that the group failed to report something new on plans to sell its stake in industrial group Elektrowatt, dealers said. Elektrowatt was up four to 507.
UBS bearer shares rose 18 to 1,275. Dealers said the share was in demand ahead of a news conference next week. UBS also gained as investors switched from CS Holding into UBS, one dealer said.
Winterthur was down five francs to 779 francs after the company said its Belgian unit merged with Belgian insurer Josi.
